chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'What is obligatory upon the one who performs Hajj on behalf of a man?' He said, 'He should mention his name at the stations and the standing places.'
And this is according to preference (al-afdal), because whoever does not do that, his Hajj is still valid in that regard.

key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ: performing Hajj on behalf of a man

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mentioning the name of the person for whom one is performing Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that while mentioning the name of the person being represented (al-mu'tamir) at the ritual stations is recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory for the validity of the Hajj, it ensures the ritual is performed with greater precision and completeness. This ruling, found in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on distinguishing between essential pillars (arkan) and recommended acts (sunan) that perfect the worship, ensuring the proxy's actions are explicitly linked to the principal. The practice underscores the importance of intentionality and specificity in proxy rituals, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj and other acts of worship.
